command: llvm-mc -triple=aarch64 -filetype=obj A64-P18-w32regoff.s -o out.o && llvm-objcopy -O binary --only-section=.text out.o out.bin
notes: Input (470 B, LF, trailing newline). Twenty instructions, one per new 32-bit row plus four register-31 rows: eight `ldr` rows (lsl/uxtw/sxtw/sxtx at #0 and #2) and the same eight `str` rows, then `ldr w0, [sp, x2]`, `ldr w0, [x1, xzr, lsl #2]`, `str w0, [sp, x2, lsl #2]` and `ldr w0, [x1, wzr, uxtw]`. Registers 0-9 keep every field value distinct. The `size = 10` rows scale the index by the 4-byte access size, so the `S = 1` rows spell `#2`; `Rt` is a `w` register while `Rn`/`Rm` stay `x` (ADR-0025 decision 4). `llvm-readobj -r` prints an empty relocation list and the source names no symbols, so no linker is involved.
source: Arm MRS LDR_32_ldst_regoff / STR_32_ldst_regoff (Rm at 16+5, option at 13+3, S at 12+1, Rn at 5+5, Rt at 0+5, size = 10), measured in EXP-0027 §1-§4
